title: Adjectives — Strong and Weak
subtitle: Gōd cyning, se gōda cyning.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Adjectives — Strong and Weak.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: Old English adjectives decline in two patterns: strong (when used without an article or after a demonstrative) and weak (after the definite article). The strong declension has distinct forms for all three genders; the weak declension is simpler. Example: gōd cyning (a good king, strong), se gōda cyning (the good king, weak).

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Strong: gōd mann (nom), gōdne mann (acc). Weak: se gōda mann (nom), þone gōdan mann (acc).
